object_types.name: Patient
object_types.definition: A person who receives medical services at the clinic, identified by a patient ID card.

source_references.excerpt: Patients book appointments. Every appointment is booked by exactly one patient, and a patient can have many appointments.
Patients have a patient ID -- it's on their card.

object_types.name: PatientId
object_types.definition: The unique identifier for a patient, printed on the patient's card.

source_references.excerpt: Patients have a patient ID -- it's on their card.

object_types.name: Doctor
object_types.definition: A medical professional who provides care to patients and holds appointments, identified by a license number.

source_references.excerpt: Each appointment is with exactly one doctor. Doctors see many patients across their appointments.
Doctors have a license number.

object_types.name: LicenseNumber
object_types.definition: The unique license number identifying a doctor.

source_references.excerpt: Doctors have a license number.

object_types.name: Appointment
object_types.definition: A scheduled visit between a patient and a doctor at the clinic, assigned an appointment number upon creation.

source_references.excerpt: Patients book appointments.
Appointments get an appointment number when they're created.

object_types.name: AppointmentNumber
object_types.definition: The unique identifier assigned to an appointment upon creation.

source_references.excerpt: Appointments get an appointment number when they're created.

object_types.name: ExamRoom
object_types.definition: A physical room at the clinic used for patient examinations, identified by a room number.

source_references.excerpt: Exam rooms have a room number.

object_types.name: RoomNumber
object_types.definition: The unique identifier for an exam room.

source_references.excerpt: Exam rooms have a room number.

object_types.name: Specialty
object_types.definition: A medical specialty (e.g., cardiology, general practice) that a doctor specializes in.

source_references.excerpt: Every doctor has exactly one specialty, like cardiology or general practice.

object_types.name: Date
object_types.definition: The calendar date of an appointment.

source_references.excerpt: Every appointment is on a date and at a time slot -- we book in fixed slots like 09:00 or 09:30.

object_types.name: TimeSlot
object_types.definition: A fixed time slot (e.g., 09:00, 09:30) for booking appointments.

source_references.excerpt: Every appointment is on a date and at a time slot -- we book in fixed slots like 09:00 or 09:30.

object_types.name: AppointmentStatus
object_types.definition: The current status of an appointment: one of scheduled, checked-in, completed, or cancelled.

source_references.excerpt: Every appointment also has a status. The status is one of: scheduled, checked-in, completed, or cancelled.
An appointment always has exactly one status from that list.

object_types.name: VisitReason
object_types.definition: The reason the patient provides for their visit when booking the appointment.

source_references.excerpt: An appointment can have a visit reason the patient gives when booking.

object_types.name: FollowUpNote
object_types.definition: A note attached by the doctor after the appointment visit.

source_references.excerpt: After the visit the doctor can attach a follow-up note. At most one follow-up note per appointment.

ambiguities.description: Identification of TimeSlot is unclear. TimeSlot is referenced as a fixed time like '09:00' or '09:30', but it is not stated whether TimeSlot has its own unique identifier (e.g., 'slot_id') or if the time string itself serves as the reference mode. If multiple occurrences of the same time slot can exist (e.g., Monday 09:00 vs. Tuesday 09:00 are different slots), then TimeSlot may need a separate identifier beyond just the time string.

ambiguities.description: Scheduling uniqueness constraint is incomplete. The rule 'every appointment is on a date and at a time slot' does not specify whether a given doctor can have multiple appointments on the same date and time, or whether a date-timeslot combination can be used by only one doctor, or whether a room can be double-booked. This affects whether composite uniqueness constraints should be applied across (Doctor, Date, TimeSlot) or (Room, Date, TimeSlot) tuples.
